name: Lin Rong San
profile: Taiwanese real estate developer, founder of Union Bank of Taiwan and of the Liberty Times newspaper group (incl. Taipei Times). Died 28 Nov 2015 in Taipei, aged 76.
notes: Deceased (2015) per Focus Taiwan obituary https://focustaiwan.tw/news/201511280016 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Rong-San. Any current Forbes listing likely reflects heirs/family; skipped rest per instructions.

name: Peter P Gassner
profile: Software engineer who worked at IBM's Silicon Valley Lab, led PeopleTools at PeopleSoft and ran technology at Salesforce before co-founding Veeva Systems in 2007. Veeva builds cloud software for the life-sciences industry and went public in 2013; Gassner remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Under Gassner, Veeva became a public benefit corporation in 2021, which made it the first public company to convert to a PBC.
deep_cut_fact: Gassner grew up in Portland, Oregon, the son of Swiss immigrants (his father had a machine shop). He earned a computer science degree from Oregon State University in 1989, and his first internship was at IBM.
notes: Low public profile but gives occasional founder interviews (Sramana Mitra, SaaStr) on vertical SaaS. The PBC claim is from Wikipedia; check it before using. Best route is Veeva PR.

name: Samwer Brothers
current_role: Oliver Samwer: CEO, Rocket Internet SE. Marc and Alexander Samwer: co-founders and investors (Rocket Internet / Global Founders Capital)
profile: Oliver, Marc and Alexander Samwer, from Cologne, sold their eBay-style auction site Alando to eBay in 1999 and later sold Jamba to VeriSign. They founded the Berlin incubator Rocket Internet in 2007, which built Zalando, Delivery Hero stakes, HelloFresh and others. Rocket went public in 2014 and was taken private in 2020. They now invest through Rocket and Global Founders Capital.
interesting_fact: Their first exit was Alando, a German auction site launched in 1999 and sold to eBay about 100 days later for roughly $43m. It became eBay Germany.
deep_cut_fact: Oliver Samwer's 1998 WHU diploma thesis, written with Max Finger, was published as the book 'America's Most Successful Startups'. It studied US startups, mainly in Silicon Valley and Massachusetts. He first visited Silicon Valley in 1995.
notes: This entry covers three brothers; Oliver is the public face and Rocket CEO. They are famously press-shy (Oliver once walked out of an interview). Rocket's general inbox is the only published route. Book record: https://stafforini.com/works/finger-1998-america-most-successful/

name: Chen Danian
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zenmen / LinkSure (WiFi Master Key)
profile: Born in 1978 and educated at Fudan University, Chen co-founded online-games company Shanda Interactive with his brother Chen Tianqiao in 1999 and served as its COO; Shanda listed on NASDAQ in 2004. He later founded Zenmen/LinkSure, maker of WiFi Master Key, a crowd-sourced Wi-Fi sharing app that reached about 900 million users.
interesting_fact: WiFi Master Key added 100 million users in three months in early 2017, passing 900 million users. It is one of the largest Wi-Fi sharing apps in the world.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Shanghai in 1996, Chen applied for commercial ChinaNET dial-up access, which took a household register booklet and 'a pile of administrative forms'. In 1998 he wrote an article for ICPCW predicting the internet's impact would be 'no less than the invention of the steam engine'.
notes: Also known as Danny Chen. The company's international PR has historically gone through PR Newswire releases. No published email found; Chinese-language outreach through Zenmen corporate communications is likely needed.

name: Mohamed Alabbar
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Eagle Hills; Chairman, Americana Restaurants; founder of Noon.com
profile: Alabbar founded Emaar Properties in 1997, which built the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall, and chaired it until 2020. Most of his fortune is his roughly 33% stake in Americana Restaurants. He now runs Abu Dhabi developer Eagle Hills, active in about 10 countries, and holds stakes in Noon.com and Zand Bank.
interesting_fact: The son of a dhow boat captain, Alabbar took his first job after college at the UAE's central bank.
deep_cut_fact: The eldest of 12 children, Alabbar studied finance and business at Seattle University's Albers School on a government scholarship (graduated 1981). In 1992 he became the founding director general of Dubai's Department of Economic Development.
notes: Media-friendly and active on social media; his own site links his X, Instagram and LinkedIn. Primary sources for the scholarship detail: BusinessWeek 2007 'The Master Builder of the Middle East' (archived) and Wikipedia.
